title: The Ghostwriter of My Own Charity
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] For six years I have funded a scholarship for orphaned students through an intermediary who does not know my name, only an account number and a standing instruction never to disclose its source.
Narrator: A literary agent recently approached me, having somehow pieced together fragments of the arrangement, and proposed a memoir framed around what she called my quiet philanthropy.
Narrator: [carefully] The advance she quoted was substantial, and I will not pretend the figure didn't tempt some petty, calculating corner of my mind for longer than I'd like to admit.
Narrator: What unsettled me wasn't the money itself but how effortlessly I could already picture the prose, the humility rehearsed just enough to read as authentic rather than performed.
Narrator: [reflective] There is a particular vanity, I've come to notice, that dresses itself in modesty, and it is far more insidious than the ordinary, unashamed kind.
Narrator: I spent an entire weekend drafting a chapter outline before the absurdity of the exercise finally caught up with me somewhere around the third revision.
Narrator: [honestly] Every sentence I wrote about giving quietly was, by the very act of being written for publication, a betrayal of the quietness it claimed to describe.
Narrator: I recognized, uncomfortably, that publishing such a book wouldn't merely reveal an old secret; it would retroactively convert years of ordinary intention into a curated narrative of virtue.
Narrator: [gently] So I declined, though not without a residue of regret that surprised me, given how certain I'd felt about my own detachment from recognition until that offer arrived.
Narrator: The scholarship continues, unnamed and unremarked upon, exactly as it always has, and the near-miss has left me warier of my own motives than I was before.
Narrator: [calmly] I no longer trust the parts of myself that insist they want nothing in return, because apparently they merely hadn't yet been offered the right price.
Narrator: Perhaps that suspicion is itself a kind of progress, a refusal to let sincerity coast on the assumption that it has already been proven and needs no further scrutiny.

quiz.question: What has the narrator funded for six years, and how?
options: A hospital wing, publicly
A mosque renovation, with his name on a plaque
A charity gala, as the main sponsor
A scholarship for orphaned students, through an intermediary who does not know his name
quiz.explanation: He has funded a scholarship for orphaned students through an intermediary who knows only an account number, not his identity.

quiz.question: What did the literary agent propose?
options: A film adaptation
A charity auction
A memoir framed around his quiet philanthropy
A newspaper interview
quiz.explanation: The agent proposed a memoir centered on what she called his quiet philanthropy.

quiz.question: What did the narrator realize while drafting the chapter outline?
options: That the advance wasn't large enough
That every sentence about giving quietly betrayed the quietness it described by being written for publication
That he had forgotten key details
That the agent was untrustworthy
quiz.explanation: He realized that writing about quiet giving for publication was itself a betrayal of that quietness.

quiz.question: What particular kind of vanity does the narrator identify?
options: Vanity that is loud and obvious
Vanity about physical appearance
Vanity that dresses itself in modesty, which he finds more insidious than the ordinary kind
Vanity related to wealth alone
quiz.explanation: He describes a vanity that dresses itself in modesty as more insidious than ordinary, unashamed vanity.

quiz.question: What effect did the near-miss have on the narrator?
options: It made him confident in his own selflessness
It left him warier of his own motives than before
It convinced him to write the memoir anyway
It ended the scholarship entirely
quiz.explanation: The experience left him more suspicious of his own motives, no longer assuming his intentions were automatically pure.

quiz.question: Why reject the memoir despite its appeal?
options: It would turn quiet service into a curated image of virtue.
It legally exposed the intermediary.
It would end the scholarship.
It made the donations invalid.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.

quiz.question: What does lingering regret reveal?
options: Recognition still appealed to motives he thought were settled.
He doubted the scholarship's value.
He needed the advance for rent.
He feared the agent's response.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.

quiz.question: How does he redefine sincerity?
options: As strict secrecy in every case.
As refusing payment for service.
As avoiding literary work.
As an intention requiring scrutiny, not a proven possession.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.

quiz.question: Why is rehearsed humility troubling?
options: It makes virtue appear performed for an audience.
It leaves out financial facts.
It confuses recipients.
It is too difficult to publish.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.

quiz.question: What practice follows his conclusion?
options: End the arrangement entirely.
Continue giving without turning it into evidence of character.
Publish it after retirement.
Ask for a smaller advance.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.
